/-!
# Erdős Problem 274

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
* [arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
* [arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
* [PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
* [arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise Cardinal

namespace Erdos274

-- TODO(callesonne): add already proved results from the wiki page

/-- An exact covering of a group `G` is a finite collection of subgroups `{H_1, ..., H_k}` and
representative `{g_1, ..., g_k}` such that the cosets `g_iH_i` are pairwise disjoint and their
union covers `G`.

Note that this differs from `Partition (α := Subgroup G)` because the covering condition there
invokes `Subgroup.sup` which is subgroup generation and thus stronger than union. This definition
is easier to use in this context than the alternative `Partition (α := Set G)`, which lacks
subgroup definitions such as `Subgroup.index`. -/
structure Group.ExactCovering (G : Type*) [Group G] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] where
  parts : ι → Subgroup G
  reps : ι → G
  nonempty (i : ι) : (parts i : Set G).Nonempty
  disjoint : (Set.univ (α := ι)).PairwiseDisjoint fun (i : ι) ↦ reps i • (parts i : Set G)
  covers : ⋃ i, reps i • (parts i : Set G) = Set.univ

/--
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type*) (_ : Group G),
    1 < ENat.card G ∧ ∃ (ι : Type*) (_ : Fintype ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι),
    1 < Fintype.card ι ∧ ∀ i j, i ≠ j → #(P.parts i) ≠ #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jostamon/erdos274-hs-abelian/blob/2ab8a2e39e7dd7836adf577b52555f069244466f/Erdos274/Main.lean"]
theorem erdos_274.variants.abelian {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G]
    (hG : 1 < Fintype.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι)
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem herzog_schonheim {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : 1 < ENat.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index := by
  sorry

end Erdos274

reformulations.difference: erdosproblems.com/274 says "if G is abelian ... the answer to the original question is no", with no finiteness assumption. The Lean variant only covers finite abelian groups (`[Fintype G] [CommGroup G]`) and adds the hypothesis `1 < Fintype.card G`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Take an infinite group G and a finite exact covering of it. B. H. Neumann's lemma says the cosets of infinite-index subgroups can be dropped from a finite cover (Mathlib: `Subgroup.leftCoset_cover_filter_FiniteIndex`). In a partition, a dropped coset would have to be empty, which is impossible. So every part has finite index. A finite-index subgroup of an infinite group has cardinality #G, so any two distinct parts have the same size and the conclusion holds automatically. Separately, `1 < Fintype.card G` follows from `1 < Fintype.card ι`, because two disjoint nonempty cosets need at least two elements. Hence "for all finite abelian G" and "for all abelian G" are equivalent. Proved in Lean as `abelianFinite_iff_abelianAll` (/workspace/review/scratch5.lean). scratch6.lean checks that the file's theorem is exactly the `AbelianFinite` shape, and that in a finite group equal sizes ⟺ equal indices.

reformulations.difference: The statement uses Mathlib's ℕ-valued `Subgroup.index`, which is 0 for infinite index. It does not assume the subgroups have finite index, whereas Margolis–Schnabel's HSC does and Wikipedia/Sun speak of "(finite) indices". It also adds the hypothesis `1 < ENat.card G`, which the sources do not state.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every part of a finite exact covering has finite index (Neumann's lemma plus disjointness). This is proved in Lean as `finiteIndex_parts`. So `index` is always the true index, and the junk value 0 can never create a spurious equality. `1 < ENat.card G` follows from `1 < Fintype.card ι` and the covering axioms (`one_lt_card_of_cover`). "∃ i ≠ j with equal index" is the negation of "the indices are pairwise distinct". Proved in Lean: `hsFile_iff_hsMaSc` shows the file's statement is equivalent to the Margolis–Schnabel form (a non-trivial partition into cosets of finite-index subgroups has two equal indices) (/workspace/review/scratch7.lean).

review.notes:
No misformalizations found. The four declarations match the cited sources, and the category tags are current.

**How each declaration matches the source**
- **`Group.ExactCovering`** is a partition of G into finitely many left cosets `reps i • parts i`. The `nonempty` field is redundant, since subgroups always contain 1.
- **`erdos_274`** states the current erdosproblems.com question literally: "If G is a group then can there exist an exact covering of G by more than one cosets of different sizes?" (page last edited 31 Oct 2025, status OPEN).
  - `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ...` has the direct polarity. It is not a negated conjecture, and the conjectured answer is False.
  - "Different sizes" has to mean pairwise distinct. Under the reading "not all equal" the answer is trivially yes: Z/4 = {0,2} ∪ {1} ∪ {3}.
- **Abelian variant and main theorem split:** the forum shows the site first said "abelian". It was generalized after a comment that Sun had already solved the abelian case. The file mirrors this: the general problem is open and the abelian variant is solved.
- **`herzog_schonheim`** matches HS as stated by Wikipedia, Sun and Margolis–Schnabel. Using left rather than right cosets makes no difference, because inversion swaps the two.

**Lean checks** (/workspace/review, all compiled):
- An `ExactCovering` of Z/2 with 2 parts exists, so the hypotheses can be satisfied.
- `finiteIndex_parts`: every part of an exact covering has finite index, so `index` never takes its junk value 0.
- `one_lt_card_of_cover`: the hypotheses `1 < ENat.card G` and `1 < Fintype.card G` are implied by the others.
- `mk_parts_eq`: in an infinite group all parts have cardinality #G. So infinite groups can never satisfy the distinct-sizes condition in `erdos_274`.
- `mk_eq_iff_index_eq`: in a finite group, equal sizes ⟺ equal indices.
- `abelianFinite_iff_abelianAll` and `hsFile_iff_hsMaSc`: the two equivalences recorded under reformulations.

Together these show that the right-hand side of `erdos_274` says a finite counterexample to HS exists. By the standard reduction to finite quotients (Korec–Znám, cited by Margolis–Schnabel), that is the same as saying any counterexample exists, which is consistent with `herzog_schonheim`.

**Status**
- The main problem and HS are both still open. The only proof claim on erdosproblems is partial: at least 18 cells would be needed.
- For the abelian variant's `formal_proof`: I did not build the external repo. Its `Group.ExactCovering` has the same fields as this file's, and its theorem statement is verbatim. The files I fetched contain no `sorry` or `axiom`.

**Cosmetic, not reported as findings**
- The abelian variant's docstring ends a declarative sentence with "?".
- The `ExactCovering` docstring calls `Partition`'s sup condition "stronger than union", which is loosely worded.

**Not read:** Erdős's own wording. The [ErGr80] scan (mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf) is image-only and no OCR tool was available, and [Er77c] is not in the Rényi archive. The file follows erdosproblems.com, which is its cited source.
